newsitem.title: CHINA: China plans to launch two satellites by early July.
newsitem.headline: China plans to launch two satellites by early July.

text.p: China plans to launch two domestically made satellites aboard its Long March 3 rockets in the next few months, an official of China Aerospace Industry Co said on Friday.
The Dongfanghong-3 (East is Red) telecommunications satellite will be launched aboard a Long March 3A rocket in May, the official said.
The Fengyun-2 meteorological satellite will be put into orbit by a Long March 3 rocket in late June or early July, she said.
Both rockets would be launched from China's Xichang satellite launch centre in southwestern Sichuan province, she said.
The Dongfanghong-3, the first large capacity communications satellite to be manufactured in China, would be the 44th satellite to be launched by China's Long March series rockets, she said.
The Fengyun-2 is the first domestically-made geostationary orbit meteorological satellite, she said by telephone.
The designed service life for the DongFangHong-3 is eight years, while the FengYun-2 is three years, she said.
No more details were released about the telecom satellite.
China has carried out 43 launches using Long March rockets with a success rate of 87 percent.
China has successfully launched 48 man-made satellites -- 38 made in China and 10 international commercial satellites.
China's space industry, once much admired for its bargain prices and record of launch successes, has been plagued by problems in recent years.
Last August, a domestic telecommunications satellite lauched aboard a Long March 3 rocket from Xichang failed to enter its proper orbit.
Last February, a new generation Long March 3B carrying an Intel satellite veered seconds after lift-off and exploded, killing six people on the ground, injuring 57 and destroying 80 homes.
